p: We are bound to thank God: The first part of the epistle, in which he rejoices that through the grace of God, they have bravely sustained all the assaults of their enemies. And in this he strengthens and encourages them, moreover showing with what gifts they must mainly fight, that is, with faith and charity, which must daily increase.
groweth exceedingly: That whereas it grew up before, it does also receive some increase every day more and more.

Which is a manifest token of: He shows the source of all true comfort, that is, that in afflictions which we suffer from the wicked for righteousness' sake, we may behold as it were in a mirror the testimony of that judgment to come, the end of which is most acceptable to us, and most severe to his enemies.
Seeing it is a righteous thing: A proof: God is just, and therefore he will worthily punish the unjust, and will do away the miseries of his people.
with us: He strengthens and encourages them also along the way by this means, that the condition both of this present state and the state to come, is common to him with them.
when the Lord Jesus shall be: A most glorious description of the second coming of Christ, to be set against all the miseries of the godly, and the triumphs of the wicked.
that know not God: There is no knowledge of God to salvation, without the Gospel of Christ.
because our testimony among you was: They are considered as children of God by the faith which they have in the Gospel, which is preached to them by the apostles.

Wherefore also we pray always for: Seeing that we have the mark set before us, it remains that we go to it. And we go to it, by certain degrees of causes: first by the free love and good pleasure of God, by virtue of which all other inferior causes work: from there proceeds the free calling to Christ, and from calling, faith, upon which follows both the glorifying of Christ in us and us in Christ.
this calling: By "calling" he does not mean the very act of calling, but that self same thing to which we are called, which is the glory of that heavenly kingdom.
all the good pleasure of his: Which he determined long ago, only upon his gracious and merciful goodness towards you.

work of faith with power: So then, faith is an excellent work of God in us: and we plainly see here that the apostle leaves nothing to free will, to make it something which God works through, as the papists dream.
